title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

errors: Defining β only on generators f^{(n)} is not enough. f ↦ Γ^n(f)∘u_n must also be a degree-n homogeneous polynomial law in f. Additivity in f, i.e. expanding Γ^n(f+g), requires a compatibility between u_n, the comultiplication Γ^{p+q} → Γ^p⊗Γ^q and Δ: roughly (u_p⊗u_q)∘Δ should equal the (p,q)-component of u_{p+q}. The page and its neighbours state only the multiplicative relation u_p u_q = C(p+q,q) u_{p+q}. This is a gap rather than an error. For flat cocommutative coalgebras with u_n = the iterated coproduct into the symmetric tensors, all conditions hold automatically.
Minor: in the Yoneda statement, C must be related to A and B (here C = A = B), and k-bilinearity plus naturality in each variable must be imposed separately. The page treats both informally.

ideas.what: A linear functor F 'respects polynomial maps' if it carries natural maps Γ^n F(X) → F(Γ^n X); degree-n polynomial maps X → Y are linear maps Γ^n X → Y
ideas.modern_name: lax morphism for the divided-power monad Γ; polynomial laws (Roby); related in spirit to strict polynomial functors

ideas.what: Lax symmetric monoidal structures on a representable functor Hom(A,-) correspond, via Yoneda, to cocommutative counital coalgebra structures on A
ideas.modern_name: Yoneda / Day-convolution description of monoidal representable functors; convolution algebra Hom(C, -)

ideas.what: Maps u_n: A → Γ^n(A) with u_0 = 1, u_1 = id, u_p u_q = C(p+q,q) u_{p+q} and σ_{pq}∘u_{pq} = Γ^p(u_q)∘u_p, making Hom(A, -) preserve PD-algebras
ideas.modern_name: divided-power (Γ-)coalgebra structure; for flat cocommutative coalgebras, the iterated coproduct landing in the symmetric tensors
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; in derived form, recent work on coalgebras for the derived Γ functor / PD operads (e.g. Brantner–Campos–Nuiten)

missed.claim: Grothendieck formulates when a representable functor Hom(A, -) preserves divided-power algebras: A must carry a family u_n: A → Γ^n A satisfying explicit axioms. This is dual to PD-algebras and is extra structure only when Γ^n differs from the invariants of A^{⊗n} (non-flat or derived settings). It anticipates the modern treatment of coalgebras over the (derived) Γ functor, but he works only at the level of axioms on flat modules.
missed.quote: Γ^n F_A(X) →? F_A(Γ^n X) ... Γ^n Hom_1(A,X) →β? Hom_1(A, Γ^n X)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as a historical anticipation: specialists in derived divided-power algebra and coalgebra would recognise it immediately, and it contains no new result.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine Yoneda-style exercises: monoidal representable functors correspond to coalgebras, plus a divided-power analogue. They are written as working notes toward the PD de Rham complex and are correct up to a minor gap. They mildly prefigure the notion of PD-coalgebra but contain nothing a specialist would find new.
transcription_corrections: Top arrow label is probably 'deg n' (degree-n polynomial map), not 'dégén'.
'Hom_1' is probably just Hom (the subscript is uncertain, possibly 'Hom_k').
In the unit line, 'k_{[?]}' is the base ring k: k → F_A(1) = Hom(A, 1); 'counité A → 1' (the arrow labelled u/ε).
The 'si X=Y=A, c'est…' line probably continues: 'id_A, id_A donne un élément de F_A(A⊗A), i.e. A → A⊗A'.
